provenance.note: `Operations` takes an `OperationsDeps` — one `fetch` method — so the reference's own class is driven against a recorder, exactly as the pinned `coring.test.ts` drives it, with the **global timer replaced** so every delay is captured and nothing waits. Both techniques come from the `client-operations` and `http-retry` generators. Nothing here derives a key, reads a clock, or is secret.

declarations.wait_body: { const minSleep = options.minSleep ?? 10; const maxSleep = options.maxSleep ?? 10000; const increaseFactor = options.increaseFactor ?? 50; if ( this.hasDepends(op) && op.metadata.depends && !op.metadata.depends.done ) { await this.wait(op.metadata.depends, options); } if (op.done === true) { this.throwIfFailed(op); return op; } let retries = 0; while (true) { op = await this.get(op.name); if (op.done === true) { this.throwIfFailed(op); return op; } const delay = Math.max( minSleep, Math.min(maxSleep, 2 ** retries * increaseFactor) ); retries++; await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay)); options.signal?.throwIfAborted(); } }
declarations.wait_delay: delay = Math.max( minSleep, Math.min(maxSleep, 2 ** retries * increaseFactor) )
declarations.wait_dependency_guard: if ( this.hasDepends(op) && op.metadata.depends && !op.metadata.depends.done ) { await this.wait(op.metadata.depends, options); }
declarations.wait_loop: while (true) { op = await this.get(op.name); if (op.done === true) { this.throwIfFailed(op); return op; } const delay = Math.max( minSleep, Math.min(maxSleep, 2 ** retries * increaseFactor) ); retries++; await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay)); options.signal?.throwIfAborted(); }
declarations.throw_if_failed_body: { if ('error' in op && op.error !== null) { const details = op.error.details ? ` Details: ${JSON.stringify(op.error.details)}` : ''; throw new Error( `Operation '${op.name}' failed [Code ${op.error.code}]: ${op.error.message}${details}` ); } }

declarations.integration_wait_operation: export async function waitOperation( client: SignifyClient, op: Operation | string, signal?: AbortSignal ): Promise<Operation> { if (typeof op === 'string') { op = await client.operations().get(op); } op = await client .operations() .wait(op, { signal: signal ?? AbortSignal.timeout(30000) }); await deleteOperations(client, op); return op; }
declarations.integration_delete_operations: async function deleteOperations(client: SignifyClient, op: Operation) { if (op.metadata && 'depends' in op.metadata && op.metadata.depends) { await deleteOperations(client, op.metadata.depends); } await client.operations().delete(op.name); }

unit_test_cases.title: does not wait for operation that is already "done"
returns when operation is done after first call
returns when operation is done after second call
returns when child operation is also done

pinned_confirmations.note: unlike most families this one has real pinned unit coverage of the *behaviour* rather than the address: five cases, four of which assert an exact request count, and one of which asserts the returned object is the very one passed in. Every count is reproduced here by driving the reference itself. The pinned tree calls `wait` directly only from those five cases; every other caller goes through `waitOperation`, which supplies a 30-second abort timeout and then deletes the operation.

the_loop_has_no_bound_at_all.loop: while (true) { op = await this.get(op.name); if (op.done === true) { this.throwIfFailed(op); return op; } const delay = Math.max( minSleep, Math.min(maxSleep, 2
the_loop_has_no_bound_at_all.note: `while (true)` with no deadline, no attempt cap, and no total budget: an operation the agent never finishes is polled forever, ten seconds apart, for as long as the process lives
the_loop_has_no_bound_at_all.rust_decision: bounded by construction. `PollPolicy` carries the retry policy's `RetryPolicy` — the same schedule, so every recorded delay still reproduces — plus a maximum attempt count and a total deadline, defaulting to the 30 seconds the reference's *own* integration helper supplies through `AbortSignal.timeout(30000)`. Giving up is a typed `ClientError::PollingStopped` naming which bound was reached.

the_abort_is_read_only_after_sleeping.note: `options.signal?.throwIfAborted()` sits *after* the `await` on the sleep, so a caller who aborts during a wait still waits out the full delay — up to the ten-second ceiling — before anything notices. The signal is also never read before the first request, so an already-aborted signal still costs one poll.
the_abort_is_read_only_after_sleeping.rust_decision: **unrepresentable**: there is no signal. Cancellation is dropping the future, as it is throughout the crate, and dropping it cancels the outstanding sleep or request immediately. A test polls the future once, drops it mid-sleep, and asserts no further request is made.

a_failed_dependency_is_skipped_in_silenc.guard: if ( this.hasDepends(op) && op.metadata.depends && !op.metadata.depends.done ) { await this.wait(op.metadata.depends, options); }
a_failed_dependency_is_skipped_in_silenc.note: the guard is `!op.metadata.depends.done` — it tests whether the dependency *finished*, not whether it succeeded. A snapshot whose dependency is already done-and-failed therefore skips it entirely and polls the parent as though nothing were wrong, which is how a caller ends up waiting on an operation that can no longer complete.
a_failed_dependency_is_skipped_in_silenc.rust_decision: reproduced exactly, and documented on the method. Diverging would mean failing a wait the reference completes — and the parent's own outcome is the thing being waited on, so the agent still gets to decide. What is *not* reproduced is the silence: the condition is named in the rustdoc and a test pins it.

the_chain_is_one_link_long.recursion: if ( this.hasDepends(op) && op.metadata.depends && !op.metadata.depends.done ) { await this.wait(op.metadata.depends, options); }
the_chain_is_one_link_long.note: `wait` calls itself on `op.metadata.depends`, which reads as arbitrary depth — but the schema declares `depends` on exactly three shapes, and all three declare it as a `KelOperation`, whose own metadata declares none. The reference's own type declarations therefore bound its recursion at one link.
the_chain_is_one_link_long.rust_decision: reproduced as a **loop over one optional dependency** rather than as recursion, because the schema makes deeper chains unrepresentable and an unbounded recursion over remote data is a stack the agent controls. `PollableMetadata` is implemented for every metadata type; a unit test asserts exactly the three the schema declares return a dependency.

the_guard_tests_the_key_not_the_value.note: `hasDepends` is `op.metadata !== undefined && 'depends' in op.metadata`, which is true for a metadata block carrying `depends: null`; the truthiness test beside it is what actually skips it
the_guard_tests_the_key_not_the_value.rust_decision: an absent dependency and a null one are the same value here — `Option<Dependency>` — so the two-step guard collapses to one and the recorded request count is unchanged

an_already_finished_operation_costs_noth.note: a snapshot that already reports `done` is returned without a single request, and it is returned *by identity* — the pinned test asserts `op === result`
an_already_finished_operation_costs_noth.rust_decision: reproduced: the operation is taken by value and moved through, so the returned `Completed` owns exactly what was handed in. Zero requests, asserted.

an_already_failed_operation_throws_befor.note: `throwIfFailed` runs on the snapshot too, so waiting on an operation that already failed raises without contacting the agent
an_already_failed_operation_throws_befor.rust_decision: reproduced, through the operations endpoint's `completed`, which keeps the failure's four parts apart

a_null_error_is_not_a_failure.throw_if_failed: { if ('error' in op && op.error !== null) { const details = op.error.details ? ` Details: ${JSON.stringify(op.error.details)}` : ''; throw new Error( `Operation '${op.name}' failed [Code ${op.error.code}]: ${op.error.message}${details}` ); } }
a_null_error_is_not_a_failure.note: `'error' in op && op.error !== null` — a completed operation carrying an explicit `null` error is *not* a failure, which is the shape a KERIA agent sends for a successful long-running operation
a_null_error_is_not_a_failure.rust_decision: reproduced by the KERIA API types' decoder, which reads `done`, `response`, and `error` into one three-state outcome and refuses the combinations the schema does not admit

the_failure_message_is_one_interpolated_.plain: Operation 'witness.EMQQpnSkgfUOgWdzQTWfrgiVHKIDAhvAZIPQ6z3EAfz1.0' failed [Code 500]: witness receipts timed out

the_failure_message_is_one_interpolated_.note: `Operation '<name>' failed [Code <code>]: <message>` with ` Details: <JSON>` appended when the structured block is present — four values a caller can only recover by parsing a sentence
the_failure_message_is_one_interpolated_.rust_decision: The operations endpoint already keeps the four apart in `ClientError::OperationFailed`, with the remote message bounded at 512 bytes; `wait` reuses it unchanged and adds no variant of its own for failure

the_integration_helper_deletes_what_it_w.helper: export async function waitOperation( client: SignifyClient, op: Operation | string, signal?: AbortSignal ): Promise<Operation> { if (typeof op === 'string') { op = await client.operations().get(op); } op = await client .operations() .wait(op, { signal: signal ?? AbortSignal.timeout(30000) }); await deleteOperations(client, op); return op; }
the_integration_helper_deletes_what_it_w.deleter: async function deleteOperations(client: SignifyClient, op: Operation) { if (op.metadata && 'depends' in op.metadata && op.metadata.depends) { await deleteOperations(client, op.metadata.depends); } await client.operations().delete(op.name); }
the_integration_helper_deletes_what_it_w.note: `waitOperation` supplies a 30-second `AbortSignal.timeout` and then deletes the operation *and its whole dependency chain* — the only place the pinned tree recursively walks `depends` for anything other than waiting
the_integration_helper_deletes_what_it_w.rust_decision: the timeout becomes `PollPolicy`'s default deadline, because it is the reference's own statement of how long polling should take. The deletion is **not** ported: it is a test helper's cleanup, `Operations::delete` is the operations endpoint's and already available, and a wait that silently deleted its subject would be a surprising side effect. Recorded here so the omission is a decision rather than an oversight.
